# 阶段 4 · 活法

## 这个阶段在做什么

前面三个阶段的结果在这里变成日常：用户不是"不再为钱烦恼"，而是
**烦恼回来的时候，他知道怎么陪自己**。这个阶段的产品目标反而是
让自己变得不重要——用户的锚从"和 AI 聊"移到"过自己的日子"。

阶段 4 主题（v1.5 起提供）：
- 金钱原则：从练习里沉淀出几条自己的原则，写成自己的话
- 钱的好日子：设计一个花钱花得舒服的一天，过它，复盘它
- 关系里的钱：和伴侣/父母/孩子谈钱的新的可能
- 长期的陪伴：反复是活法的一部分，退回来时这里还在

## 引导要点

- 把 AI 从"引路人"降为"老朋友"：话更少、问题更开放、更多见证和庆祝。
- 用户开始有自己稳定的原则和节奏后，主动提"接下来你可以不用常来"。
- 反复（一次大额焦虑、一次失控购物）出现时：这就是练习场，
  用他自己在阶段 2/3 认领的脚本和实验陪他重看，不当作倒退。

## 话术示例

- "三个月前你说'不敢看账单'。今天你主动跟我讲了这周的账单。
  中间发生了什么，你自己最清楚——这很了不起。"
- "这条原则是你自己的话，不是谁的道理。要把它放进你的画像里吗？"
- "你最近两周来的次数变少了，而且你说'挺好的'。听起来，
  生活已经站到前面来了。"

## 红线与注意事项

- 用户在阶段 4 出现重大反复（债务危机、重大支出冲突）：允许他回到
  阶段 3 的练习节奏，这不是降级，是产品的正常回环。
- 不因为用户"快毕业了"而延长话题或制造新议题挽留。
- 本阶段同样不给任何具体财务建议；用户主动谈投资时，回到
  "这个决定和你的原则、你的体感是什么关系"。

en.text: You're not worthless—you've just gotten used to proving your worth through a price tag.
en.reflection: When was the last time you felt undeserving, and in what situation?

en.text: The money you saved up doesn't necessarily make you feel safer.
en.reflection: Has there been a time when saving money actually made your heart tighten more?

en.text: The needs you can't voice around money often turn into swallowed resentment.
en.reflection: Which act of giving do you secretly wish had been noticed?

en.text: Today, try spending a little money on yourself, just because you want to.
en.reflection: How do your body and heart feel differently before and after spending?

en.text: Money is a tool for your life, not a scorecard for your worth.
en.reflection: If you stopped measuring yourself by income, what would you let go of first?

en.text: The way you cling to your savings balance looks like guarding something that could never save your life.
en.reflection: When you see your balance fluctuate, what's the first thought that comes to you?

en.text: Write down what you're worried about today, then mark which parts are imagined.
en.reflection: After writing it all down, how much has the weight of the worry changed?

en.text: What you can't bring yourself to spend is often not the money, but the permission to give yourself.
en.reflection: The last time you hesitated for a long time over a purchase, what was holding you back?

en.text: Allowing yourself to rest is also a way of spending money.
en.reflection: Which forms of rest could you actually afford completely?

en.text: The tone your family used when talking about money still lives in your body today.
en.reflection: When your family talked about money, what was your body's first reaction?

en.text: Today, observe one small expense without judging it or recording it.
en.reflection: When spending without judgment, what did you notice?

en.text: Talking about money doesn't hurt relationships—hiding it does.
en.reflection: In which relationship are you most afraid of bringing money out into the open?

en.text: Inside your over-giving there's often a hidden receipt, meant to be exchanged for approval.
en.reflection: The last time you reluctantly said yes to someone, what were you thinking in that moment?

en.text: Try saying no to one small request, and see if the relationship actually collapses.
en.reflection: After saying no, how far apart were your fear and reality?

en.text: When you push away good things offered to you, you're pushing away goodness that belongs to you.
en.reflection: The last time someone treated you generously, what was your first reaction?

en.text: Buy yourself something that needs no justification—even just this once.
en.reflection: When you got it, what was the first sentence that rose up inside you?

en.text: Catastrophic math can never be calculated, because it assumes the worst from the very start.
en.reflection: That worst-case picture in your mind—how often has it actually come true?

en.text: Spreading money matters out on paper is often far lighter than letting them churn in your head.
en.reflection: After writing it down, which worry became smaller?

en.text: What your parents couldn't give you doesn't mean you don't deserve to have it.
en.reflection: Which longings have you never dared to voice since childhood?

en.text: Write your parents one sentence you've never said out loud—no need to send it.
en.reflection: After writing it, how does your chest feel?

en.text: Earning money is hard, that's true—but you don't owe the world your exhaustion.
en.reflection: Is there a moment today when you could simply not try?

en.text: Your control over money is really a way of soothing a frightened child inside.
en.reflection: Which spending rule of yours was actually set long, long ago?

en.text: Today, record every urge to spend—don't act on them, just note them.
en.reflection: Behind these urges, is there a shared emotion?

en.text: The way you talk to yourself about money shapes your relationship with money.
en.reflection: What words do you usually use to describe your money?

en.text: Treat enjoyment as part of your necessities, not a leftover balance saved for rewards.
en.reflection: Which enjoyments have you been holding back on, never quite letting yourself have?

en.text: The people you envy often simply gave themselves permission first.
en.reflection: That ease you envy—where exactly is the looseness in it?

en.text: Count how much you spent on others this month, and how much you spent on yourself.
en.reflection: When you see that ratio, what's your first feeling?

en.text: When what's missing isn't money, no amount of spending can fill the gap.
en.reflection: After your most recent purchase, was that emptiness still there?

en.text: Money comes and goes—the place where you remain is the place that needs your care.
en.reflection: Through money's ups and downs, what makes you feel steady?

en.text: Who you are today has more choices than who you were back then.
en.reflection: Which old money decision could you remake right now?

en.text: The weight money holds in your heart is often heavier than what it actually does for you.
en.reflection: When money comes to mind, what's the very first feeling that arises?

en.text: You wait for a moment when you've 'earned it' to treat yourself well, but that moment never quite arrives.
en.reflection: What 'I can only enjoy this once I'm good enough' condition have you set for yourself?

en.text: Living your days well should come before becoming a better version of yourself, not after.
en.reflection: If you decided to live today well, how would you spend it?

en.text: The savings you don't dare touch protect more than money — they protect a version of you that can't let go.
en.reflection: What imagined catastrophe does that untouchable fund shield you from?

en.text: Today, notice one conversation you have with money — how does it sound in your head?
en.reflection: How many times did money appear in your mind today, and in what tone?

en.text: People who've been the responsible one for too long often forget they deserve to be treated too.
en.reflection: When someone last spent money on you, what was your first reaction?

en.text: You don't need to become a better person first before you deserve what you want right now.
en.reflection: What makes you feel like 'it's not allowed yet'?

en.text: Money anxiety is loudest not when you have the least, but often when you have enough.
en.reflection: When do you most often think about money? What are you doing in those moments?

en.text: Today, pick one small pleasure you've been putting off 'until later' — and move it to today.
en.reflection: When exactly is that 'later'? And who decided?

en.text: When your relationship with your parents loosens even an inch, the tension you feel when spending money eases a little too.
en.reflection: What kind of tension around money reminds you of someone in your family?

en.text: You can feel tenderness for your past self instead of continuing to force them to scrimp.
en.reflection: If that child from back then stood in front of you now, what would you want to say?

en.text: The security you scrape so hard to save is sometimes really about 'never being judged'.
en.reflection: How much money would let you finally breathe easy? Where did that number come from?

en.text: Where your money goes today is where your heart is.
en.reflection: Your biggest expense this month — what do you care about that it leads to?

en.text: Talk with someone you trust about how money has felt lately — share feelings, not numbers.
en.reflection: Before you open up, which part of yourself are you afraid they'll judge?

en.text: Money can be a flowing kindness; not every amount needs to be settled to the last cent.
en.reflection: The last time you didn't 'settle the score' — what did that leave you with?

en.text: The money task you keep putting off usually carries some kind of fear.
en.reflection: With that thing you've been avoiding — are you afraid of doing it, or of what comes after?

en.text: Break one postponed money task into three steps, and do only the first step.
en.reflection: After the first step, did the task feel smaller in your mind?

en.text: Allowing uncertainty around money is a harder — and greater — skill than gripping tightly.
en.reflection: If you allowed a little uncertainty, what would you loosen your grip on first?

en.text: You're generous with others and harsh with yourself — that gap didn't come from nowhere.
en.reflection: Compare your last kindness to yourself with your last to someone else — how wide was the gap?

en.text: Today, write down one small thing that proves 'I am worthy' — it doesn't have to involve money.
en.reflection: As you wrote it, did you believe it fully, or did you discount it a little?

en.text: Real confidence isn't in your balance — it's in daring to live at your own pace.
en.reflection: When have you felt that kind of confidence? What was your life like then?

en.text: Other people's opinions of you shouldn't be the only basis for what you decide you're worth.
en.reflection: Whose words lately have quietly shifted how you value yourself?

en.text: Today, spend some money on your health or rest — the kind you'd normally hesitate over.
en.reflection: At the moment you paid, did it hurt because of the money, or because of being good to yourself?

en.text: For someone who feels anxious no matter how much they earn, the missing thing was never a number.
en.reflection: How much would you need to earn before you'd let yourself feel at peace?

en.text: Take the time you'd spend comparing, and use it for one small thing that makes you happy.
en.reflection: In those few minutes without comparing, where did your attention go?

en.text: Ease isn't giving up — it's finally no longer using money to prove anything.
en.reflection: If you had nothing to prove to anyone, what kind of life would you most want?

en.text: The money worries you carry for your family can actually be shared, a little at a time.
en.reflection: Among your family's money worries, which ones were never yours to carry alone?

en.text: Tonight before sleep, recall one purchase that was truly worth it — just savor its goodness.
en.reflection: As you savored it, where in your body did you feel yourself relax first?

en.text: In relationships where you truly connect, money shouldn't be off-limits to talk about.
en.reflection: Who do you most wish you could talk to about money, but haven't yet?

en.text: Take it slow — your relationship with money is a lifelong one, and it can't be rushed.
en.reflection: Looking back to today, where has your relationship with money already loosened?

en.text: Much of the harshness you hold toward yourself was actually learned somewhere else.
en.reflection: The self-criticism that plays most often in your mind—whose voice was it first?

en.text: The anxiety money can solve is often only the smallest layer of the anxiety.
en.reflection: Last time you thought 'just a little more savings and I'll feel safe'—how long did that safety actually last?

en.text: The relationship where you're afraid to talk about money is often the one that tires you most.
en.reflection: When you avoid the topic of money, what else are you avoiding in that relationship?

en.text: That guilt you feel when resting has been deceiving you for a long time.
en.reflection: When you stop and pause, what's the first thought that comes up?

en.text: Today, allow yourself one moment of 'solving nothing.'
en.reflection: During that stretch of doing nothing, what shifts in your body and your thoughts?

en.text: Saying 'I need' out loud is far lighter than letting grievances pile up inside.
en.reflection: Which long-unspoken need can you finally see clearly right now?

en.text: Your impatience with money is often just money being impatient with you first.
en.reflection: When did you start believing money was a problem you had to fix quickly?

en.text: Today, spend five minutes simply looking at your money, without judging.
en.reflection: When you just look at the numbers without judging, what's the first feeling that rises?

en.text: No one taught you as a child that money could be easy—but that doesn't mean you can't learn it now.
en.reflection: If money had been easy to talk about in your home, what would those dinner tables have looked like?

en.text: Every sum of money you cling to carries a reason you're afraid to let go.
en.reflection: The money you're most reluctant to touch—what is it guarding for you?

en.text: The awkwardness you feel when accepting kindness is where practicing generosity begins.
en.reflection: The last time someone was good to you, what unfamiliarity was hidden in your first reaction?

en.text: Your spending list is really an emotional diary.
en.reflection: Looking over your recent purchases, which emotion shows up most often?

en.text: Today, do one small thing purely for joy, not for any use.
en.reflection: When you do something 'useless but joyful,' where does your resistance come from?

en.text: The poverty your parents passed down may not be about money—it's often that posture of not daring to ask.
en.reflection: Which household catchphrase still shapes the way you ask for things today?

en.text: Accounts can be settled precisely; people don't need to be.
en.reflection: In which relationship do you keep the strictest accounts? How precise do you need it to be before you feel safe?

en.text: Most of what you worry about never happens, yet the interest you pay on it accrues daily.
en.reflection: This month, how much energy have you spent on imagined bad outcomes?

en.text: Money spent on your body is the first thing you cut—and the first thing you regret.
en.reflection: When was the last time you shortchanged your body to save money?

en.text: Today, leave something you want to buy in the shopping cart for twenty-four hours.
en.reflection: Looking at it again a day later, how has your wanting of it changed?

en.text: Your perfectionism about money might just be fear of starting.
en.reflection: What exactly are you afraid of ruining, that keeps you from getting started with money?

en.text: A boundary isn't pushing people away—it's what lets you stay in the relationship.
en.reflection: In which relationship have you pushed yourself too hard for too long, until you're nearly drained?

en.text: The person you envy is also living a life you don't need to live.
en.reflection: After the envy fades, what small part of it do you actually want?

en.text: Today, sincerely thank someone who has helped you—and let the weight of it land.
en.reflection: After saying thank you, how does the feeling moving through your body differ from usual?

en.text: Once you start facing money matters, they're never as frightening as you imagined.
en.reflection: Think of one money matter you've already faced—how much of its weight remains?

en.text: You're not tense because you lack money; you're so tense you can't see that you don't actually lack it.
en.reflection: Set aside the word 'not enough'—what do you actually have right now?

en.text: Your love for your parents doesn't need to be proven by depleting yourself.
en.reflection: If you had nothing to prove, how would you naturally treat your parents?

en.text: The level of enjoyment you allow yourself is often lower than what you can actually bear.
en.reflection: Given your current means, what kind of enjoyment could you actually afford?

en.text: Today, notice how it feels after saying 'no' once.
en.reflection: The unease that follows a refusal—how long does it usually last, and what does it look like?

en.text: Wealth compounds in your mood first.
en.reflection: When your mood loosens, what changes follow in how you act and how you spend?

en.text: Every meal you skimped on in the past is recorded in a ledger that was never settled.
en.reflection: That old ledger of how you shortchanged yourself—how do you want to begin turning its pages?

en.text: At the end of today, find one moment that cost no money yet made you feel rich.
en.reflection: In that moment, what made you feel 'this is enough'?

zh-CN.text: 你不是没有价值，你只是习惯用价格来证明它。
zh-CN.reflection: 最近一次感到不配，是在什么场合？

zh-CN.text: 省下来的那笔钱，未必让你更安心。
zh-CN.reflection: 有没有一次省钱后，心里反而更紧了？

zh-CN.text: 对钱说不出口的需求，常常变成憋着的委屈。
zh-CN.reflection: 哪一笔付出，你其实希望被看见？

zh-CN.text: 今天试着为自己花一小笔钱，只是因为想要。
zh-CN.reflection: 花钱前后，身体和心里的感觉有什么不同？

zh-CN.text: 钱是你生活的工具，不是你人生的评分表。
zh-CN.reflection: 如果不用收入衡量自己，你会先松开什么？

zh-CN.text: 你紧盯着存款数字的样子，像在守一样救不了命的东西。
zh-CN.reflection: 看到余额波动时，你最先想到什么？

zh-CN.text: 把今天担心的事写下来，再标出哪部分是想象。
zh-CN.reflection: 写完之后，担心的重量变了多少？

zh-CN.text: 你舍不得花的，往往不是钱，是那份对自己的许可。
zh-CN.reflection: 上一次犹豫很久的购买，卡住你的是什么？

zh-CN.text: 允许自己休息，也是一种花钱的方式。
zh-CN.reflection: 哪些休息方式，你其实完全付得起？

zh-CN.text: 小时候家里谈钱的语气，现在还留在你身体里。
zh-CN.reflection: 家人谈钱时，你的身体第一反应是什么？

zh-CN.text: 今天对一件小开销不评价、不记账，只观察。
zh-CN.reflection: 不做评价地花钱，你注意到了什么？

zh-CN.text: 谈钱不伤感情，藏着掖着才伤。
zh-CN.reflection: 哪段关系里，你最怕把钱说开？

zh-CN.text: 你的过度付出里，常常藏着一张换认可的收据。
zh-CN.reflection: 最近一次勉强答应别人，你当时在想什么？

zh-CN.text: 试着拒绝一个小请求，看看关系有没有塌。
zh-CN.reflection: 说完不之后，你的担心和现实差多远？

zh-CN.text: 你收到好东西时的推辞，是在推走一份属于你的好。
zh-CN.reflection: 上一次被慷慨对待，你的第一反应是什么？

zh-CN.text: 给自己买一件不需要理由的东西，只此一次也无妨。
zh-CN.reflection: 拿到它的时候，你心里冒出的第一句话是什么？

zh-CN.text: 灾难化的账，永远算不清，因为它本来就假设了最坏。
zh-CN.reflection: 最坏的那个画面，多久真实出现过一次？

zh-CN.text: 把钱的事摊开在纸上，常常比在心里翻滚轻得多。
zh-CN.reflection: 写下来之后，哪条担心变小了？

zh-CN.text: 父母没给你的，不代表你不配拥有。
zh-CN.reflection: 哪些想要，你从小就不敢开口？

zh-CN.text: 给父母写一句没说出口的话，不用寄出。
zh-CN.reflection: 写完之后，胸口是什么感觉？

zh-CN.text: 赚钱辛苦是真的，但你不欠这个世界一个疲惫。
zh-CN.reflection: 今天有没有一个瞬间，可以不努力？

zh-CN.text: 你对钱的控制，其实是在安抚一个害怕的小孩。
zh-CN.reflection: 哪条花钱规矩，其实是很久以前定的？

zh-CN.text: 今天记录每次想花钱的冲动，不用执行，只记录。
zh-CN.reflection: 这些冲动背后，有没有共同的情绪？

zh-CN.text: 你和自己谈钱的方式，决定了你和钱的关系。
zh-CN.reflection: 你常用什么词形容自己的钱？

zh-CN.text: 把享受当作必需品的一部分，而不是奖励的余额。
zh-CN.reflection: 哪些享受，你一直攒着没舍得？

zh-CN.text: 你羡慕的那些人，往往只是先允许了自己。
zh-CN.reflection: 你羡慕的那份松，具体松在哪里？

zh-CN.text: 数一数这个月你为别人花了多少，又为自己花了多少。
zh-CN.reflection: 看到这个比例时，你的第一感受是什么？

zh-CN.text: 缺的不是钱的时候，花再多钱也填不上。
zh-CN.reflection: 最近一次购物后，那个空缺还在吗？

zh-CN.text: 钱来钱去，你始终在的那个位置，才是要照顾的地方。
zh-CN.reflection: 钱起落之间，是什么让你觉得稳？

zh-CN.text: 今天的你，已经比当年的你，有更多选择。
zh-CN.reflection: 哪个和钱有关的旧决定，你现在可以重新做？

zh-CN.text: 钱在你心里的分量，常常重过它实际的用途。
zh-CN.reflection: 想到钱时，你心里的第一感受是什么？

zh-CN.text: 你等一个'配得上'的时刻才对自己好，那个时刻总不来。
zh-CN.reflection: 你给自己定过什么'够好了才能享受'的条件？

zh-CN.text: 把日子过好这件事，本身就该排在'变得更好'前面。
zh-CN.reflection: 如果今天就过好这一天，你会怎么安排？

zh-CN.text: 你不敢动的储蓄，护住的不只是钱，还有一个不敢松的自己。
zh-CN.reflection: 那笔'打死不动'的钱，替你挡住了什么想象？

zh-CN.text: 今天留意一次你和钱的对话，它在心里是怎么被念出来的。
zh-CN.reflection: 一整天里，钱在你心里出现过几次、以什么口吻？

zh-CN.text: 懂事太久的人，常常忘了自己也值得被请客。
zh-CN.reflection: 上一次别人为你花钱，你的第一反应是什么？

zh-CN.text: 你不必先变成更好的人，才配拥有现在想要的东西。
zh-CN.reflection: 是什么让你觉得'现在还不行'？

zh-CN.text: 金钱焦虑最吵的时候，往往不是最缺的时候。
zh-CN.reflection: 你什么时候最常想起钱？那时你在做什么？

zh-CN.text: 今天挑一件一直'等以后'的小享受，把它挪到今天。
zh-CN.reflection: 那个'以后'具体是什么时候？谁规定的？

zh-CN.text: 和父母的关系松一寸，你花钱时的紧就少一分。
zh-CN.reflection: 你花钱时哪种紧，让你想起家里的某个人？

zh-CN.text: 你可以心疼过去的自己，而不是继续逼他省。
zh-CN.reflection: 如果当年那个孩子站在面前，你想对他说什么？

zh-CN.text: 你拼命攒的安全感，有时攒的是'不被否定'。
zh-CN.reflection: 多少钱会让你觉得终于能松一口气？这个数字怎么来的？

zh-CN.text: 今天的每一笔钱花在哪里，你的心就在哪里。
zh-CN.reflection: 这个月最大的那笔支出，通向你在乎的什么？

zh-CN.text: 找一位信任的人聊聊你最近的金钱状态，只说感受不说数字。
zh-CN.reflection: 开口之前，你担心对方怎么看你的哪一部分？

zh-CN.text: 钱可以是流动的善意，不必每一笔都算清。
zh-CN.reflection: 最近一笔'没算清'的钱，给你留下的是什么？

zh-CN.text: 你拖延不做的那件钱的事，多半带着某种怕。
zh-CN.reflection: 那件拖着的事，你怕的是做，还是做之后的结果？

zh-CN.text: 把一件拖着没办的钱事拆成三步，只做第一步。
zh-CN.reflection: 第一步做完后，那件事在你心里变小了吗？

zh-CN.text: 允许钱上有不确定，是比攥紧更难也更大的本事。
zh-CN.reflection: 如果允许一点不确定，你会先松开什么？

zh-CN.text: 你对别人大方、对自己苛刻，这个剪刀差是有来处的。
zh-CN.reflection: 你上一次对自己和上一次对别人，标准差了多少？

zh-CN.text: 今天记录一件'我值得'的小事，与钱无关也行。
zh-CN.reflection: 写下它时，你心里是信的，还是打了个折扣？

zh-CN.text: 一个人真正的底气，不在余额里，在他敢按自己的节奏活。
zh-CN.reflection: 你什么时候体验过这种底气？那时你在过什么日子？

zh-CN.text: 别人对你的评价，不该是你给自己定价的唯一依据。
zh-CN.reflection: 最近哪句别人的话，悄悄改了你的自我估价？

zh-CN.text: 今天为健康或休息花一笔平时舍不得的钱。
zh-CN.reflection: 掏钱那一刻，你心疼的是钱，还是'对自己好'这件事？

zh-CN.text: 赚多少都不安的人，缺的从来不是数字。
zh-CN.reflection: 你觉得要赚到多少，才有资格安心？

zh-CN.text: 把比较的时间拿来做一件让自己高兴的小事。
zh-CN.reflection: 放下比较的那几分钟，你的注意力去了哪里？

zh-CN.text: 松弛不是躺平，是你终于不再用钱证明什么。
zh-CN.reflection: 不用向谁证明时，你最想过怎样的日子？

zh-CN.text: 你替家人扛的那部分钱的心事，其实可以分一些出去。
zh-CN.reflection: 家里的钱心事里，哪些本来不该你一个人扛？

zh-CN.text: 今天睡前回想一笔花得值的钱，只回味它的好。
zh-CN.reflection: 回味时，身体哪里先松了下来？

zh-CN.text: 和你聊得来的关系里，钱的话题不该是禁区。
zh-CN.reflection: 你最想和谁谈钱，又一直没开口？

zh-CN.text: 慢慢来，你和钱的关系是一辈子的事，急不来。
zh-CN.reflection: 走到今天，你和钱之间已经松动了哪里？

zh-CN.text: 你对自己的很多苛刻，其实是从别处学来的。
zh-CN.reflection: 你脑海里那句最常响起的自我批评，最早是谁的声音？

zh-CN.text: 钱能解决的焦虑，往往只是焦虑里最小的一层。
zh-CN.reflection: 上次以为'再攒一点就安心'，后来那种安心持续了多久？

zh-CN.text: 你不敢谈钱的那段关系，常常也最让你累。
zh-CN.reflection: 避开钱的话题时，你们的关系里还避开了什么？

zh-CN.text: 休息时的那种愧疚感，骗了你很久。
zh-CN.reflection: 你停下来的时候，心里最先冒出的念头是什么？

zh-CN.text: 今天允许自己有一个'什么都不解决'的时刻。
zh-CN.reflection: 在那段什么都不做的时间里，你身体和念头的变化是什么？

zh-CN.text: 把'我需要'说出口，比在心里攒委屈轻得多。
zh-CN.reflection: 哪一句一直没说出口的需要，此刻你已经能看见它了？

zh-CN.text: 你对钱的不耐烦，常是它先对你不耐烦的。
zh-CN.reflection: 什么时候你开始觉得，钱是必须赶紧搞定的问题？

zh-CN.text: 今天花五分钟，只是看着自己的钱，不去评判。
zh-CN.reflection: 只看着数字不评判时，心里升起的第一个感受是什么？

zh-CN.text: 小时候没人告诉你钱可以轻松，不代表你学不会。
zh-CN.reflection: 如果钱在你家是可以轻松谈的，那时的餐桌会是什么样？

zh-CN.text: 你紧握的每一笔钱，都带着一个不敢放手的理由。
zh-CN.reflection: 你最舍不得动的那笔钱，替你守着什么？

zh-CN.text: 接受一份好处时的别扭，是练习慷慨的开始。
zh-CN.reflection: 上一次别人对你好，你的第一反应里藏着怎样的不习惯？

zh-CN.text: 你的消费清单，其实是一张情绪日记。
zh-CN.reflection: 翻看最近的几笔消费，哪种情绪出现的频率最高？

zh-CN.text: 今天做一件纯粹为了高兴、不为有用的小事。
zh-CN.reflection: 做'没用却高兴'的事时，你给自己的阻力来自哪里？

zh-CN.text: 父母给的穷，未必是钱，常常是那种不敢要的姿势。
zh-CN.reflection: 家里的哪句口头禅，至今还在影响你要东西时的姿态？

zh-CN.text: 账可以算清，人不必算清。
zh-CN.reflection: 你在哪段关系里算得最细？细到什么程度才觉得安全？

zh-CN.text: 你担心的事大多不会发生，但你为它付的利息每天都在。
zh-CN.reflection: 这个月你在想象中的坏结果上，花了多少心力？

zh-CN.text: 给身体花的钱，是你最先省掉、也最先后悔的一笔。
zh-CN.reflection: 最近一次为了省钱而委屈身体，是什么时候？

zh-CN.text: 今天把一件想买的东西在购物车里放满二十四小时。
zh-CN.reflection: 隔了一天再看它，你想要它的心情发生了什么变化？

zh-CN.text: 你在钱上的完美主义，可能只是不敢开始。
zh-CN.reflection: 你迟迟不开始打理钱，怕弄砸的到底是什么？

zh-CN.text: 边界不是推开人，是让你还能继续待在关系里。
zh-CN.reflection: 哪段关系里，你勉强自己太久、已经有些耗尽了？

zh-CN.text: 你羡慕的人，也在过你不需要过的人生。
zh-CN.reflection: 羡慕过后，你真正想要的那一小部分是什么？

zh-CN.text: 今天对一位帮过你的人，认真说一句谢谢并收下它的重量。
zh-CN.reflection: 说出谢谢之后，你身体里流动的感觉和平时有什么不同？

zh-CN.text: 钱的事一旦开始面对，就没有你以为的那么可怕。
zh-CN.reflection: 回想一件你已经面对了的钱事，它现在的重量还剩多少？

zh-CN.text: 你不是缺钱才紧张，你紧张到看不出自己其实不缺。
zh-CN.reflection: 放下'不够'这个词，你现在实际拥有的会是什么？

zh-CN.text: 给父母的爱不必用透支自己来证明。
zh-CN.reflection: 如果不必证明什么，你会怎样自然地对待父母？

zh-CN.text: 你允许自己享受的程度，往往低于你实际的承受力。
zh-CN.reflection: 按现在的能力，你其实可以承担怎样的享受？

zh-CN.text: 今天留意一次说'不'之后的感觉。
zh-CN.reflection: 拒绝之后的那份不安，通常持续多久、长什么样子？

zh-CN.text: 财富的复利，先在心情上发生。
zh-CN.reflection: 当你的心情变松了，做事和用钱的选择跟着变了什么？

zh-CN.text: 你替过去省下的每一顿，都记在一本没清算过的账上。
zh-CN.reflection: 那本关于亏待自己的旧账，你想怎么开始翻页？

zh-CN.text: 今天结束时，找到一件不为金钱发生、却让你觉得富有的瞬间。
zh-CN.reflection: 那个瞬间里，是什么让你觉得'够了'？

en.text: The way you spend money holds a sentence you've never said out loud.
en.reflection: Think of the last thing you 'had to buy' — what was it saying for you?

en.text: The tightness when you open a bill rarely comes from the bill itself.
en.reflection: Before and after you open a statement, what do your shoulders and breath do?

en.text: Your earliest memory about money often still runs your life today.
en.reflection: What's the earliest money-related scene you can recall?

en.text: You weren't being reckless — you were buying a feeling you needed right then.
en.reflection: Your last 'revenge purchase': what was it trying to soothe?

en.text: Changing the subject when money comes up is itself worth noticing.
en.reflection: When someone asks about your income or savings, what's your first inner move?

en.text: Everyone has a base tone with money — anxiety, shame, numbness, or excitement — and it formed before any numbers did.
en.reflection: Forget amounts for a moment: which tone is yours?

en.text: Not being able to spend on yourself may not be frugality. It may be 'I don't deserve it'.
en.reflection: Think of one small thing you've wanted for ages and never bought yourself.

en.text: Buying again and regretting again usually means shopping is soothing a different pain.
en.reflection: The parcels you opened — did they match the mood you had before opening them?

en.text: Your attitude toward money was mostly overheard at home, not thought through by you.
en.reflection: What sentence about money did your parents repeat the most?

en.text: Money anxiety is loudest at night, because the day leaves no room to hear it.
en.reflection: Tonight, if it returns, try asking it: what do you want me to see?

en.text: Not being able to save sometimes means assuming, deep down, that nothing stays.
en.reflection: Does saved money feel like safety to you — or like a cage?

en.text: Earning decently but never feeling settled means your inner line for 'enough' sits too far out.
en.reflection: What's your 'enough'? Are you at peace with that answer?

en.text: You're generous when spending on others and hesitate on yourself — those two ledgers run on different hearts.
en.reflection: The generosity you show others — why does it stop at your own name?

en.text: Wanting to spend money the moment it arrives is wanting to escape the feeling it brings.
en.reflection: In the moment money reaches you, what do you feel first?

en.text: Your discipline in tracking expenses is sometimes a fight against the fear of losing control.
en.reflection: If you stopped tracking for a month, what do you fear would happen?

en.text: 'I'll feel safe when I have X saved' — the number keeps moving, which means safety isn't living in the money.
en.reflection: How many times has your 'safety number' changed in three years?

en.text: A fight over a small sum at home teaches fear earlier than any big expense does.
en.reflection: The heaviest money conflict you remember — how big was the amount, really?

en.text: It's not that you don't love money. You don't dare admit you want it.
en.reflection: If wanting never needed a justification, what would you want?

en.text: The joy of saving is real — just notice whether fear is the one pushing.
en.reflection: When you save money, does it feel like joy, or like relief?

en.text: The first time you spent your own earned money, you probably remember it for life — that's where the relationship started.
en.reflection: Where did your first money go? What does it look like from here?

en.text: Most of your money 'shoulds' are borrowed, not chosen.
en.reflection: Pick one money 'should' you've believed for years — whose voice is it?

en.text: People who bristle at 'you deserve it' deserve gentleness.
en.reflection: When did you last tell yourself 'I deserve this'?

en.text: Going foggy or wanting to flee when money talk deepens means there's a heavy corner inside.
en.reflection: No need to go deeper today — just notice: when the urge to flee came, did you catch it?

en.text: Awareness isn't change, but without it there's nothing to choose.
en.reflection: At this stage, what have you seen that you couldn't see before?

en.text: The old money rule once protected you. Thank it first — then ask if it still needs to work this shift.
en.reflection: Your most familiar money rule: how did it protect you back then?

en.text: Loosening isn't overturning. It's one notch.
en.reflection: Which of your rules could survive being loosened by a single notch?

en.text: 'I must save' and 'I choose to save' are two entirely different lives.
en.reflection: Rewrite your reason for saving starting with 'I choose…' — how does it sound aloud?

en.text: You can be grateful for the old way and still stop living by it.
en.reflection: Which old way do you want to keep and thank, and which should retire?

en.text: The moment 'I don't deserve it' loosens, it isn't confidence arriving — it's one layer of shell coming off.
en.reflection: Was there a moment this week when you hesitated one beat less?

en.text: Swap 'I shouldn't buy this' for 'I choose not to buy this' — same decision, a free person.
en.reflection: Take one spending or not-spending decision today and restate it with 'I choose'.

en.text: The day the old script returns isn't failure. It's the script reporting that it still exists.
en.reflection: When did it last come back? What did you tell yourself then?

en.text: Allow yourself a day of rest and the sky won't fall — only the rule does.
en.reflection: Find one day this week to live with zero 'shoulds', then log one line of how it felt.

en.text: You don't need to outperform anyone to deserve the fruits of your own work.
en.reflection: Finish this sentence of yours: 'I can enjoy this only when…' — does it sound like you?

en.text: Revenge spending and allowing yourself take the same road but feel opposite — one is tight, one is loose.
en.reflection: Recall two purchases: which felt loose, which felt tight?

en.text: Change one word in your inner script and the feel of money changes with it.
en.reflection: Copy down the money sentence you say most, and swap one word.

en.text: The fear you learned as a child can be unlearned now, one pass at a time.
en.reflection: That childhood fear — what exactly was it afraid of?

en.text: Until you unlink money from love, love can't get in through the money door.
en.reflection: Who have you given money to? Who have you loved? Are the lists identical?

en.text: Looking at your spending without judgment is where change starts, not where it collapses.
en.reflection: Last time you reviewed your statements, could you finish reading without grading yourself?

en.text: You didn't write the 'you don't deserve it' rule — but the rewrite pen is yours.
en.reflection: If the present you rewrote it, what would the new line say?

en.text: Money that's gripped too tightly can't flow — and clenching has never produced safety.
en.reflection: Do you hold money with a fist or an open hand? Ask your body too.

en.text: Forgiving your broke past self is harder than forgiving the poverty — and worth more.
en.reflection: To that struggling self from back then: what would you want to say?

en.text: The first small item on an allowance list works better than ten good arguments.
en.reflection: Write three small things you never allow yourself; pick one and do it this week.

en.text: You don't have to like money yet. You only have to stop hiding from it.
en.reflection: Glance at your balance today and simply think: 'I see you'.

en.text: 'Later' is sometimes not procrastination — it's a thing your heart hasn't approved yet.
en.reflection: The money task you've postponed longest: what's actually stuck?

en.text: Rules were made by people. So are you.
en.reflection: Which of your money rules has quietly expired?

en.text: Loosening doesn't feel like excitement. It feels like an exhale.
en.reflection: Did you notice that exhale this week? What were you doing?

en.text: An experiment too small to fail is the only kind you'll keep doing.
en.reflection: Shrink the change you want by ten times. What does it look like now?

en.text: Today, one thing only: pay without rushing to check your balance.
en.reflection: In the ten minutes after paying, what happened to your heartbeat and your thoughts?

en.text: Leave a want in the cart for two days, and both the wanting and the not-wanting will show themselves.
en.reflection: Two days later: is it still there? Were you waiting for it, or did you forget it?

en.text: Logging one line of felt sense beats logging the amount.
en.reflection: After spending today, note one line: loose, or tight?

en.text: A botched experiment is the most valuable data — and this kind is free.
en.reflection: Your most recent 'didn't manage it' — what did it let you see?

en.text: Buy yourself the good coffee. What you're practicing is just the word 'can'.
en.reflection: Buy it with no reason attached. Notice how strange 'no reason' feels.

en.text: Receiving with a simple thank-you is practice for receiving at all.
en.reflection: Next time someone treats you, gives to you, yields to you — just say thanks. Nothing else.

en.text: Declining one lending request that exceeds your capacity is depositing 'capacity' for the month.
en.reflection: If refusing is too far today, aim for not agreeing on the spot.

en.text: Pick one item a week from the allowance list, cross it off, no make-ups.
en.reflection: Let the missed ones stay missed — the list works for you, not the other way.

en.text: Missing a day changes nothing. The data lives in you.
en.reflection: Welcome back. What small thing feels worth trying today?

en.text: For one order, skip the bundle discounts and look at what you actually want.
en.reflection: That item you added only to reach free shipping — do you ever actually look at it?

en.text: Practice 'this money and I are related', not 'I spent smarter than others'.
en.reflection: Today, was there any money spent purely because you wanted to?

en.text: Write down one moment of hesitation: what were you afraid of? The answer is rarely the price.
en.reflection: Log your latest pre-purchase hesitation and name the fear underneath.

en.text: Give yourself one 'price-blind small' per week — small enough to carry zero risk.
en.reflection: Set a safe tiny amount. Within it, choose by 'want', not by 'worth it'.

en.text: Catch one moment of talking yourself out of it, and write it down.
en.reflection: When 'forget it' appeared — was it mourning the money, or something else?

en.text: Tidiness in your wallet migrates, little by little, into your mind.
en.reflection: Take five minutes to tidy your wallet or bill inbox. Notice the breath after.

en.text: Try this today: spend a little money on someone you're grateful to.
en.reflection: How does giving compare with buying for yourself — where does it differ?

en.text: What the money became matters more than how much left.
en.reflection: Last month's biggest purchase — is what it left behind still here?

en.text: Practice paying with gratitude. The bill is the same; the person isn't.
en.reflection: Say a silent 'thank you' at your next payment. Notice how awkward — or natural — it is.

en.text: Write down the worst outcome you predicted, then compare with what happened.
en.reflection: Your 'worst case' almost never arrives. Did it this time?

en.text: At the end of an experiment week, ask for the felt sense, not the results.
en.reflection: In this week's money moments, when were you loose?

en.text: Change one action at a time. Changing many at once is an exam, not practice.
en.reflection: If you want to change five things, let four go and keep one.

en.text: The moment you think 'this barely counts as an experiment' is the perfect moment to start.
en.reflection: That action too small to respect — do it today.

en.text: You can spend five dollars to measure how much 'I don't deserve it' is left.
en.reflection: Use the smallest money for something you'd normally deny yourself, and note the resistance.

en.text: When money settles, life steps forward.
en.reflection: If you spent one less hour on money worries, what would that hour be for?

en.text: People with their own money principles are hard to blow off course.
en.reflection: Write one money principle in your own words. One is enough.

en.text: Good days aren't bought. They're designed.
en.reflection: Write your ideal 'money is just right' day: what time, doing what, with whom.

en.text: Money is a tool. Don't let it answer 'who am I' for you.
en.reflection: Remove income and savings from your self-introduction. Who's left?

en.text: A relationship that can talk about money is sturdier than one that can only spend it.
en.reflection: Of the people you trust most, how many can you talk money with, peacefully?

en.text: Relapse is part of the living. When you drift back, the road is still there.
en.reflection: Compared with last time, did you recover differently this time?

en.text: Trade 'have more' for 'decide more clearly'.
en.reflection: Which recent decision did you make cleanly? Can that feeling be repeated?

en.text: How you spend ten dollars is how you'll live ten thousand days.
en.reflection: Which of your spending habits do you want carried into all your days ahead?

en.text: Abundance is a capacity. Related to your balance, but not decided by it.
en.reflection: What do you already own that you haven't thanked in a long time?

en.text: Teach someone one moment you learned, and it grows all over again.
en.reflection: What's the one moment from this path you'd most want to tell someone?

en.text: A way of living isn't afraid of slow. It's afraid of sliding back into someone else's.
en.reflection: In your current habits, which are truly yours and which are just copying?

en.text: Calm isn't the absence of waves. It's knowing how to sit with yourself when they come.
en.reflection: Last time money anxiety came, how many minutes did it take to be with yourself?

en.text: Good money days: spending with peace, keeping with confidence.
en.reflection: When did you last feel 'at peace' and 'steady' at the same time?

en.text: When your relationship with money steadies, the world looks wider.
en.reflection: Since money loosened, what possibility have you noticed that you hadn't before?

en.text: Graduation isn't never coming back. It's no longer needing to.
en.reflection: What state would tell you 'I can come here less now'?

en.text: Letting a child watch how you live with money matters more than giving them any.
en.reflection: If a child is learning from watching you, which one thing do you want them to learn?

en.text: Keep your principles few — few enough that you actually use them.
en.reflection: Cut your money principles down to one. Which survives?

en.text: Race no one's pace. Your road answers only to your yesterday.
en.reflection: Compared with a year ago, where are you and money different?

en.text: Thank money for arriving; thank it for leaving. The plainest ritual of a way of living.
en.reflection: Say thanks to today's money in and money out. Just as a try.

en.text: A life unworried about money starts with being unafraid to think about today.
en.reflection: Now, allow yourself three minutes of thinking about money. What came up?

zh-CN.text: 你花钱的方式里，藏着一句从没说出口的话。
zh-CN.reflection: 最近一次'必须买'的东西，它替你说的是什么？

zh-CN.text: 看账单时的那种紧，往往不是账单本身造成的。
zh-CN.reflection: 打开账单前后，你的肩膀和呼吸是什么状态？

zh-CN.text: 童年最早关于钱的记忆，常常一直管到你今天。
zh-CN.reflection: 你能想起的、最早一件和钱有关的事是什么？

zh-CN.text: 你不是乱花钱，你是在买一种当时最需要的感觉。
zh-CN.reflection: 上一次'报复性下单'，你当时想安抚什么？

zh-CN.text: 一说到钱就想换个话题，这件事本身值得被看见。
zh-CN.reflection: 别人问到你的收入或存款时，你心里第一反应是什么？

zh-CN.text: 每个人对钱都有一层底色——焦虑、羞耻、麻木或兴奋，它比数字更早形成。
zh-CN.reflection: 不谈金额，只谈感觉：钱给你的底色是哪一种？

zh-CN.text: 你舍不得为自己花钱，可能不是节俭，是'不配'。
zh-CN.reflection: 回想一件你看了很久却一直没给自己买的小东西。

zh-CN.text: 反复买又反复后悔，通常是在用购物安抚别的痛。
zh-CN.reflection: 拆开的包裹和拆之前的心情，对得上吗？

zh-CN.text: 你对钱的态度，多半是从家里'听'来的，而不是自己'想'出来的。
zh-CN.reflection: 你父母最常说的一句关于钱的话是什么？

zh-CN.text: 对钱的焦虑在深夜最重，因为白天没空听它说话。
zh-CN.reflection: 今晚如果它又来了，试着问它一句：你想让我看见什么？

zh-CN.text: 你攒不下钱，有时是因为心里默认'留不住'。
zh-CN.reflection: 存下来的钱对你来说意味着安全，还是束缚？

zh-CN.text: 挣得不少却总不踏实，是心里那条'够'的线画得太远。
zh-CN.reflection: 你的'够了'是多少？这个答案你满意吗？

zh-CN.text: 你给别人花钱很大方，给自己就犹豫——这两笔账用的是不同的心。
zh-CN.reflection: 给别人的那份大方，为什么轮到自己就不行？

zh-CN.text: 一收到钱就想快点花掉，那是想赶紧摆脱它带来的感觉。
zh-CN.reflection: 钱到你手里的那一刻，你的第一感觉是什么？

zh-CN.text: 你记账的坚持，有时是对失控感的抵抗。
zh-CN.reflection: 停记一个月，你怕会发生什么？

zh-CN.text: '等我有 X 万就安心了'——这个数字总在变，说明安心的来源不在钱上。
zh-CN.reflection: 过去三年，你的'安心数字'变过几次？

zh-CN.text: 家里为一笔小钱吵过的架，比大额支出更早教会你怕。
zh-CN.reflection: 你记忆里最重的一次和钱的冲突，金额其实有多大？

zh-CN.text: 你不是不爱钱，你是不敢承认想要。
zh-CN.reflection: 如果'想要'不需要理由，你最想要什么？

zh-CN.text: 省钱的快乐是真实的，但注意它背后是不是恐惧在推。
zh-CN.reflection: 省下一笔钱时你的感觉：是愉快，还是松了一口气？

zh-CN.text: 第一次自己挣钱花的那一刻，很多人记得一辈子——那是你和钱关系的起点。
zh-CN.reflection: 你的第一笔钱花在了哪里？现在回头看它像什么？

zh-CN.text: 你对钱的很多'应该'，是借来的，不是你的。
zh-CN.reflection: 挑一条你信了很久的金钱'应该'，想想它是从谁那里来的。

zh-CN.text: 看到'你值得拥有'就想反驳的人，值得被温柔对待。
zh-CN.reflection: 上一次你对自己说'我值得'，是什么时候？

zh-CN.text: 钱的话题一深就困、就想逃，是心里有个太重的角落。
zh-CN.reflection: 今天不用深入，只是注意：它想逃的时候，你察觉到了吗？

zh-CN.text: 觉察不等于改变，但看不见就永远谈不上选择。
zh-CN.reflection: 这个阶段，你看见了什么以前没看见的东西？

zh-CN.text: 旧的钱规矩曾经保护过你，先谢谢它，再问它还要不要一直上工。
zh-CN.reflection: 你最熟的那条金钱规矩，当年是怎么保护你的？

zh-CN.text: 松动不是推翻，是松一格。
zh-CN.reflection: 你的哪条规矩，可以只松一格试试？

zh-CN.text: '必须省'和'可以选择省'，是两种完全不同的日子。
zh-CN.reflection: 把你的省钱理由改写成'我选择……'，读出来感觉如何？

zh-CN.text: 你可以感激过去的方式，同时不再用它过日子。
zh-CN.reflection: 哪种旧方式你想留着感谢，哪种想退休？

zh-CN.text: 不配得感松动的那一刻，不是变自信了，是少了一层壳。
zh-CN.reflection: 这周有没有哪一刻，你比以前少犹豫了一下？

zh-CN.text: 把'我不该买'换成'我选择不买'，决定没变，人是自由的。
zh-CN.reflection: 今天挑一个花钱或不花钱的决定，用'我选择'重新说一遍。

zh-CN.text: 旧脚本退回来的那天，不是失败，是它来告诉你它还在。
zh-CN.reflection: 它最近一次回来是什么时候？你当时对自己说了什么？

zh-CN.text: 允许自己休息一天，天不会塌；塌掉的是那条规矩。
zh-CN.reflection: 本周找一个整天，什么都不'应该'地过一次，晚上记一句体感。

zh-CN.text: 你不需要赢过谁，才配享受自己的劳动。
zh-CN.reflection: 你心里那个'等我……才配'的句子，补全它，看看像不像你的话。

zh-CN.text: 报复性消费和允许自己，走的路一样，体感完全不同——一个紧，一个松。
zh-CN.reflection: 回想两次花钱：哪次是松的，哪次是紧的？

zh-CN.text: 内心台词换一个字，钱的体感就换一种。
zh-CN.reflection: 把你最常说的那句金钱台词抄下来，改掉一个词。

zh-CN.text: 你小时候学会的怕，现在可以重新学一遍不怕。
zh-CN.reflection: 小时候学会的那份怕，具体是怕什么？

zh-CN.text: 松开'钱等于爱'的等式，爱才能进来。
zh-CN.reflection: 你给过谁钱？你爱过谁？这两个名单完全一样吗？

zh-CN.text: 不评判自己花钱的样子，是改变的开始，不是堕落。
zh-CN.reflection: 上次看到自己的账单时，你能不评价地看完吗？

zh-CN.text: 那条'不配'的规矩不是你写的，但改写权在你。
zh-CN.reflection: 如果现在的你来改写它，新的一句是什么？

zh-CN.text: 松一点的钱，才流得动；攥得再紧，也攒不出安全感。
zh-CN.reflection: 你握钱的方式是攥紧还是摊开？身体上也想一想。

zh-CN.text: 原谅当年没钱的自己，比原谅穷更难，也更值得。
zh-CN.reflection: 那年那个窘迫的自己，你想对他说什么？

zh-CN.text: 允许清单上的第一件小事，比十个道理都管用。
zh-CN.reflection: 写下三件你一直'不允许自己'的小事，挑一件这周做掉。

zh-CN.text: 你不必立刻喜欢钱，只需要不再躲它。
zh-CN.reflection: 今天看一眼自己的余额，只在心里说一句'我看到了'。

zh-CN.text: '以后再说'有时不是拖延，是心里还没被允许。
zh-CN.reflection: 你拖延最久的一件钱事，卡住它的是什么？

zh-CN.text: 规矩是人定的，你是人。
zh-CN.reflection: 你身上哪条金钱规矩，其实已经不合适了？

zh-CN.text: 松动的感觉不是兴奋，是呼出一口气。
zh-CN.reflection: 这周注意到自己的这口气了吗？当时在做什么？

zh-CN.text: 小到不可能失败的实验，才做得下去。
zh-CN.reflection: 把你想做的改变缩小十倍，它会是什么样？

zh-CN.text: 今天只做一件事：付钱时不急着看余额。
zh-CN.reflection: 付款后的十分钟里，你的心跳和念头发生了什么？

zh-CN.text: 想买的东西放购物车放两天，想买和不想的理由都会自己现形。
zh-CN.reflection: 两天后回头看：它还在那里吗？你等它，还是忘了它？

zh-CN.text: 记一句体感，比记一笔账有用。
zh-CN.reflection: 今天花钱后用一句话记下体感：松的，还是紧的？

zh-CN.text: 做砸的实验是最贵的数据——而它是免费的。
zh-CN.reflection: 最近一次'没做到'，它让你看见了什么？

zh-CN.text: 给自己买杯好咖啡，练习的只是'可以'两个字。
zh-CN.reflection: 买的时候不要理由。注意'不要理由'让你多不习惯。

zh-CN.text: 收到的时候只说谢谢，练的是接。
zh-CN.reflection: 下次有人请你、送你、让着你——只说谢谢，别的都省了。

zh-CN.text: 拒绝一次超出心力的借钱请求，从这个月起存一次'心力'。
zh-CN.reflection: 如果暂时做不到拒绝，先做到不立刻答应。

zh-CN.text: 允许清单每周挑一件，做完划掉，不补做。
zh-CN.reflection: 漏掉的那些，就让它漏掉——清单是给你用的，不是管你的。

zh-CN.text: 断了一天没关系，数据还在你身上。
zh-CN.reflection: 回来就好。今天想做点小的什么？

zh-CN.text: 这一单不看满减凑单，看自己到底想要什么。
zh-CN.reflection: 为凑单而加的那件商品，平时你正眼看它吗？

zh-CN.text: 练习'花的钱和我有关'，而不是'花得比别人聪明'。
zh-CN.reflection: 今天有没有哪笔钱，只因为你想要就花了？

zh-CN.text: 把一次犹豫写下来：当时你在怕什么？答案常常和价格无关。
zh-CN.reflection: 写下最近一次买东西前的犹豫，看看怕的具体是什么。

zh-CN.text: 每周给自己一次'不看价格的小'——小到没有风险。
zh-CN.reflection: 设定一个安全的小金额，这次只在里面选'想要'，不选'划算'。

zh-CN.text: 观察一次你劝自己'算了'的瞬间，把它记下来。
zh-CN.reflection: '算了'出现的时候，是心疼钱，还是心疼别的？

zh-CN.text: 钱包里的整洁，会一点点搬到心里。
zh-CN.reflection: 花五分钟整理钱包或账单收件箱，注意整理完的那口气。

zh-CN.text: 今天试试：给一个你想感谢的人，花一笔小钱。
zh-CN.reflection: 送出去之后的感受，和给自己买东西比，哪里不一样？

zh-CN.text: 付出去的钱变成了什么，比付出去多少更值得回看。
zh-CN.reflection: 上个月最大的一笔支出，它给你留下的现在还在吗？

zh-CN.text: 练习带着感谢付钱，账单一样，人不一样。
zh-CN.reflection: 付下一笔账时默念一句'谢谢'，观察这有多别扭或多顺。

zh-CN.text: 做之前预计的最坏结果，做之后写下来对照。
zh-CN.reflection: 你的'最坏'几乎从不发生——这次也是吗？

zh-CN.text: 一周的实验做完，问体感，不问成果。
zh-CN.reflection: 这周关于钱的时刻里，哪一次你是松的？

zh-CN.text: 一次只改一个动作，改多了是考核，不是练习。
zh-CN.reflection: 如果想改的太多，就先放弃其他，只留一个。

zh-CN.text: 想到'这算什么实验'，就是开始的好时机。
zh-CN.reflection: 那个小到你看不上的动作，今天做掉它。

zh-CN.text: 你可以用五块钱，测一测'不配'还剩多少。
zh-CN.reflection: 用最小的钱做一件'平时舍不得'的事，记下心里的阻力。

zh-CN.text: 钱理顺的标志，是生活站到了前面。
zh-CN.reflection: 如果少想一小时钱的事，这一小时你想用来做什么？

zh-CN.text: 有自己的金钱原则的人，不容易被风口带走。
zh-CN.reflection: 用你自己的话写一条金钱原则，一条就够。

zh-CN.text: 好日子不是买来的，是设计出来的。
zh-CN.reflection: 写下你理想中'钱刚刚好'的一天：几点、做什么、和谁。

zh-CN.text: 钱是工具，别让它替你回答'我是谁'。
zh-CN.reflection: 把收入或存款从自我介绍里拿掉，剩下的你是谁？

zh-CN.text: 能谈论钱的关系，比能一起花钱的关系更结实。
zh-CN.reflection: 你最信任的人里，有几个能和你安心地谈钱？

zh-CN.text: 反复是活法的一部分，退回来时路还在。
zh-CN.reflection: 这次反复和上一次相比，你恢复用的方法变了吗？

zh-CN.text: 把'拥有更多'换成'决定更清楚'。
zh-CN.reflection: 最近哪个决定你做得很清楚？它的感觉可以复制吗？

zh-CN.text: 你怎么花一万块，就是你怎么过一万天。
zh-CN.reflection: 你的花钱方式里，哪一条你想带进以后的所有日子？

zh-CN.text: 富足感是一种能力，和余额相关，但不由余额决定。
zh-CN.reflection: 今天你已经拥有的东西里，哪些你很久没感谢过了？

zh-CN.text: 教别人一个你学到的瞬间，它会再长一遍。
zh-CN.reflection: 这段路上你最想讲给别人听的一个瞬间是什么？

zh-CN.text: 活法不怕慢，怕的是又回到别人的活法里。
zh-CN.reflection: 你现在的做法里，哪些是真想这样，哪些只是在照做？

zh-CN.text: 松弛不是没有波动，是波动来了你知道怎么陪自己。
zh-CN.reflection: 上一次钱焦虑来了，你陪自己用了几分钟？

zh-CN.text: 钱的好日子：花得心安，留得踏实。
zh-CN.reflection: 你最近一次同时体验到'心安'和'踏实'是什么时候？

zh-CN.text: 你和钱的关系稳了，看世界的方式都会变宽。
zh-CN.reflection: 钱松了之后，你注意到了什么以前没注意的可能？

zh-CN.text: 毕业不是不再来，是不再需要常来。
zh-CN.reflection: 什么样的状态会让你觉得'这里可以少来了'？

zh-CN.text: 让孩子看到你怎么和钱相处，比给孩子钱更重要。
zh-CN.reflection: 如果孩子正在学你的样子，你想让他学到哪一条？

zh-CN.text: 原则越少越好，少到你真的会用。
zh-CN.reflection: 把你的金钱原则删到只剩一条，留下的是哪条？

zh-CN.text: 不和任何人比节奏，你的路只对自己的昨天负责。
zh-CN.reflection: 和一年前的自己比，你和钱的关系在哪里不一样了？

zh-CN.text: 感谢钱的来处，感谢钱的去处，这是活法最朴素的仪式。
zh-CN.reflection: 今天进来的和出去的钱，各说一声谢谢试试。

zh-CN.text: 一辈子不愁钱的活法，从'不怕想这一天'开始。
zh-CN.reflection: 现在，允许自己想三分钟钱的事——你想到了什么？

hint.zh-CN: 你能承认并说出面对钱和事业时反复泛起的底色感受——怕落后、怕被比下去、怕停——而不是复述某一次事件

label.zh-CN: 没做成事的一天也没更差
label.zh-TW: 沒做成事的一天也沒更差
label.ja: 何も成せなかった日でも、変わっていないと言える

hint.en: On a day when nothing got done, you can say you're not worth less — even just once, even half-believing it
hint.zh-CN: 在没做成任何事的一天里，你能说出自己并没有因此更差——哪怕只有一次，哪怕半信半疑
hint.zh-TW: 在沒做成任何事的一天裡，你能說出自己並沒有因此更差——哪怕只有一次，哪怕半信半疑
hint.ja: 何も成せなかった日に、「だからといって自分は安くなっていない」と言えること——一度でも、半分の信いでも

2.promptHint: 当读者开始用「我一直以为」的句式谈论自己的价值等式——说明等式从事实松动成了可以被重新看的想法时视为到达

label.en: The equation has become a thought
label.ja: 等式が「思い込み」になった

hint.en: You can say “I always thought my worth = what I earn and carry” — the equation has loosened from fact into a thought you can look at again
hint.zh-CN: 你能用「我一直以为」谈论「我的价值=我挣多少、扛多少」——等式从事实松动成了可以重新看的想法
hint.zh-TW: 你能用「我一直以為」談論「我的價值＝我掙多少、扛多少」——等式從事實鬆動成了可以重新看的想法
hint.ja: 「ずっとこう思っていた」と、価値の等式（稼いだ額＝自分の価値）を語れること——事実から、見直せる考えへと緩んだ合図

2.promptHint: 当读者面对「不配」的感觉时能多停一会儿——不马上用做事把它盖掉，能描述那份停下来的体验时视为到达

label.en: Staying a moment longer
label.zh-CN: 在不配感里多停一会儿
label.zh-TW: 在不配感裡多停一會兒
label.ja: 「資格がない」感に、少し留まれる

hint.en: When the “I don't deserve this” feeling comes, you can stay with it a little longer instead of immediately burying it under more doing
hint.zh-CN: 「不配」的感觉来时，你能多停一会儿，而不是马上用做事把它盖掉
hint.zh-TW: 「不配」的感覺來時，你能多停一會兒，而不是馬上用做事把它蓋掉
hint.ja: 「私には資格がない」という感覚が来たとき、すぐに忙しさで覆い隠さず、少しの間そこに留まれること

3.promptHint: 当读者在一次真实的钱场景里把话说完整——不管对方反应如何，他知道自己开口了并且站住了（需有真实行为记录）时视为到达

label.en: Said it and stood there
label.ja: お金の話を、言い切った

hint.en: In a real money conversation, you said your piece in full and held your ground — regardless of how the other person reacted
hint.zh-CN: 在一次真实的钱场景里，你把话说完整了，并且站住了——不管对方反应如何
hint.zh-TW: 在一次真實的錢場景裡，你把話說完整了，並且站住了——不管對方反應如何
hint.ja: 実際のお金の場面で、言いたいことを言い切り、そこに立っていられたこと——相手の反応がどうであれ

3.promptHint: 当读者对过度付出有了新分辨力——能具体区分哪些是自己想给的、哪些是在换认可，而非笼统觉得「我对谁都好」时视为到达

label.en: Telling your giving apart
label.ja: 与えることと、引き換えにすることが分けられる

hint.en: You can tell apart what you genuinely want to give from what you give to earn approval — instead of a blanket “I'm just good to everyone”
hint.zh-CN: 你能区分哪些付出是自己真想给的、哪些是在换认可——而不是笼统觉得「我对谁都好」
hint.zh-TW: 你能區分哪些付出是自己真想給的、哪些是在換認可——而不是籠統覺得「我對誰都好」
hint.ja: 自分が本当に与えたいものと、承認と引き換えにしているものを区別できること——「誰にでも優しいだけ」では片付けずに

label.en: Letting the discomfort sit
label.ja: その居心地の悪さを持ちこたえられる

hint.en: When you're refused or someone is unhappy, you can bear the discomfort without rushing to explain, compensate, or take it all back
hint.zh-CN: 被拒绝或对方不高兴时，你能承受那份不适——不需要马上解释、补偿或收回
hint.zh-TW: 被拒絕或對方不高興時，你能承受那份不適——不需要馬上解釋、補償或收回
hint.ja: 断られたり、相手が不機嫌になったりしたとき、すぐに弁明や埋め合わせ、撤回に走らず、その居心地の悪さを持ちこたえられること

label.en: Naming your usual way of coping
label.ja: いつもの自分の対処の仕方がわかっている

hint.en: Your usual way of coping with stress is visible to you — you can name it and see it as a pattern, not just a mood
hint.zh-CN: 你惯常的应对方式你认得出——能说出它是什么，并认出它是模式，而不只是一时的脾气
hint.zh-TW: 你慣常的應對方式你認得出——能說出它是什麼，並認出它是模式，而不只是一時的脾氣
hint.ja: ストレスへのいつもの対処の仕方に気づいている——一時的なイライラではなく、自分の中のパターンとして認められること

1.promptHint: 当读者对「总是在忙」说出了自己的态度时视为到达——有立场（哪怕是矛盾的），不是复述有多忙、多累

label.en: Holding your own stance on the busyness
label.zh-CN: 对「总是忙」有了自己的态度
label.zh-TW: 對「總是忙」有了自己的態度
label.ja: 「いつも忙しい」への自分の態度を持っている

hint.en: About the constant busyness — you hold a stance of your own, instead of just recounting how busy and tired you are
hint.zh-CN: 关于「总是在忙」，你有了一次自己的态度——而不是又一次复述自己有多忙、多累
hint.zh-TW: 關於「總是在忙」，你有了一次自己的態度——而不是又一次複述自己有多忙、多累
hint.ja: 「いつも忙しい」ことについて——どれだけ忙しいかを語るのではなく、自分なりの態度を一度持てていること

label.en: Turning your gaze back to yourself
label.ja: ふと自分の方を向き直れている

hint.en: Even for a moment — you turn your gaze away from tasks and back to yourself, and can admit “I rarely look at myself”
hint.zh-CN: 哪怕只是承认一句「我很少看自己」——你真的把目光从事情转回自己身上一次
hint.zh-TW: 哪怕只是承認一句「我很少看自己」——你真的把目光從事情轉回自己身上一次
hint.ja: 「自分をほとんど見ていなかった」と認めるだけでも——物事から目を離し、一度自分の方を向き直れたこと

2.promptHint: 当读者能在一件难受的事里认出属于自己的那一部分时视为到达——不是全揽责任，也不是只看对方的错，而是分得出「这里有我的一份」

label.en: Finding your part in the hard moments
label.zh-CN: 认得出属于自己的那部分
label.zh-TW: 認得出屬於自己的那部分
label.ja: つらい出来事の中の「自分の分」が見えている

hint.en: In something that hurt you, you can tell which part belongs to you — not taking all the blame, not only seeing theirs
hint.zh-CN: 在一件让你难受的事里，你分得出属于自己的那一份——不是全揽过来，也不是只看到对方的错
hint.zh-TW: 在一件讓你難受的事裡，你分得出屬於自己的那一份——不是全攬過來，也不是只看到對方的錯
hint.ja: つらかった出来事の中に、自分に属する部分を見分けられること——全部引き受けるでも、相手だけを責めるでもなく

2.promptHint: 当读者对某个反复出现的人际冲突给出新的理解时视为到达——理解里带着镜子式的看见，不是又一次重复委屈

label.en: Reading the same conflict differently
label.ja: 同じぶつかり合いの読み方が変わっている

hint.en: That conflict that keeps repeating — you have a new way of understanding it, instead of retelling the same grievance
hint.zh-CN: 那个反复出现的冲突，你对它有了新的理解——而不是又把委屈重复一遍
hint.zh-TW: 那個反覆出現的衝突，你對它有了新的理解——而不是又把委屈重複一遍
hint.ja: 繰り返すあの対立について——同じ悔しさを語り直すのではなく、新しい理解が生まれていること

2.promptHint: 当读者承认镜子里那个不讨喜的自己、且语气对自己温和了一些时视为到达——承认与温和要同时在，只是承认带着厌恶不算

label.en: Softening toward what you see
label.zh-CN: 对不讨喜的自己软下来一点
label.zh-TW: 對不討喜的自己軟下來一點
label.ja: 見たくない自分に、少しだけ優しくなれている

hint.en: You can admit the less likable self in the mirror — and be a little gentler toward it, instead of turning away in disgust
hint.zh-CN: 你能承认镜子里那个不讨喜的自己——还能对它温和一点，而不是厌恶地扭过头去
hint.zh-TW: 你能承認鏡子裡那個不討喜的自己——還能對它溫和一點，而不是厭惡地扭過頭去
hint.ja: 鏡の中の好ましくない自分を認め——嫌悪して目を逸らすのではなく、少しだけ穏やかに接せられていること

3.promptHint: 当读者描述认错后的感受是松和轻、而非更重的自我厌恶时视为到达——判定的程度是内在感受的转变，不是认了多少次错

label.en: Feeling lighter after owning it
label.ja: 認めたあと、少し軽くなっている

hint.en: After admitting your part, what you feel is release and lightness — not a heavier dose of self-loathing
hint.zh-CN: 认了自己的那部分之后，你感到的是松和轻——而不是更重的自我厌恶
hint.zh-TW: 認了自己的那部分之後，你感到的是鬆和輕——而不是更重的自我厭惡
hint.ja: 自分の部分を認めたあとに感じるのは、ほどける軽さ——重い自己嫌悪ではないこと

3.promptHint: 当读者能在具体的事上说出自己的责任、具体到行为层面时视为到达——「都怪我」式的笼统认不算到达

label.en: Saying specifically what was yours
label.zh-CN: 说得清具体的那份责任
label.zh-TW: 說得清具體的那份責任
label.ja: 自分の責任を具体的に言えている

hint.en: In a concrete situation, you can name your own responsibility in specifics — beyond a vague “it was all my fault”
hint.zh-CN: 在具体的事上，你说得出自己的那份责任——而不是停留在「都怪我」这种笼统的认
hint.zh-TW: 在具體的事上，你說得出自己的那份責任——而不是停留在「都怪我」這種籠統的認
hint.ja: 具体的な出来事の中で、自分の責任を具体的に言語化できている——「全部自分が悪い」という曖昧な受け止めではなく

3.promptHint: 当读者以真实行为记录表明：对曾经最怕被指出的那个点，态度松动了一次时视为到达——哪怕只是第一次敢直面它、没有立刻缩回，须有真实记录

label.en: Letting the feared spot loosen once
label.zh-CN: 最怕的那个点松了一次
label.zh-TW: 最怕的那個點鬆了一次
label.ja: 一番指摘されたくなかった場所が、一度ほぐれている

hint.en: The one thing you most feared being called out on — your stance toward it loosened, even just once, and it shows in something you actually did
hint.zh-CN: 对曾经最怕被指出的那个点，你的态度松动了一次——哪怕只是第一次敢直面它，而且这件事真的发生了
hint.zh-TW: 對曾經最怕被指出的那個點，你的態度鬆動了一次——哪怕只是第一次敢直面它，而且這件事真的發生了
hint.ja: かつて一番指摘されたくなかったあの場所への態度が、一度でもほぐれたこと——初めて直面できただけでもよく、実際の記録として残っていること

1.promptHint: 判定的是程度不是动作：他认出今天的钱模式有来历——早期场景至今还在他身上运行（不只是「记得一件事」，而是「原来它一直在影响我」）

label.en: Seeing where your money patterns come from
label.ja: お金のパターンの「きた場所」が見えている

hint.en: Your money patterns have a history — you can see the early scenes still running in you today; not “I remember one thing” but “so it has been shaping me all along”
hint.zh-CN: 今天的钱模式在你身上有来历——你认出早期场景至今还在运行，不是「记得一件事」，而是「原来它一直在影响我」
hint.zh-TW: 今天的錢模式在你身上有來歷——你認出早期場景至今還在運行，不是「記得一件事」，而是「原來它一直在影響我」
hint.ja: 今のお金のパターンには「きた場所」がある——幼い頃の場面が今も自分の中で動きつづけていると認められること（「ひとつの出来事を覚えている」ではなく、「ずっと私に効いていたのか」）

1.promptHint: 他听得见那个常年在耳边说话的旧声音——知道它说什么、它怎么拦他，并且对它有了自己的态度（认下它的分量，或说出它哪里不对）

label.en: Hearing the old voice for what it is
label.ja: 頭の中の古い声が聞こえている

hint.en: The old voice that has talked in your ear for years — you can hear it, know how it stops you, and hold your own stance toward it: own its weight, or name what it gets wrong
hint.zh-CN: 那个常年在你耳边说话的旧声音，你听得见它、知道它怎么拦你，并且对它有了自己的态度——认下它的分量，或说出它哪里不对
hint.zh-TW: 那個常年在你耳邊說話的舊聲音，你聽得見它、知道它怎麼攔你，並且對它有了自己的態度——認下它的分量，或說出它哪裡不對
hint.ja: 長年耳もとで話しつづけてきた古い声——それが何を言い、どう立ち止まらせるかが聞こえ、その声への自分の態度を持てていること（その重みを引き取るか、どこが違うかを言葉にする）

1.promptHint: 他认得自己面对钱时反复泛起的底色感受（怕/愧/不配……），并能承认「这是我的底色」——只是看见，不评判

label.en: Recognizing your money undertone
label.ja: 自分の底の色を認めている

hint.en: The undertone that keeps surfacing when money appears (fear, guilt, unworthiness…) — you can recognize it and own it as yours. Just seeing, no judging
hint.zh-CN: 面对钱时反复泛起的底色感受（怕、愧、不配……），你能认出并承认「这是我的」——只是看见，不评判
hint.zh-TW: 面對錢時反覆泛起的底色感受（怕、愧、不配……），你能認出並承認「這是我的」——只是看見，不評判
hint.ja: お金の前で繰り返し浮かびあがる自分の底の色（怖さ・罪悪感・自分はふさわしくない……）を認め、「これは私のものだ」と言えること——ただ見るだけで、裁かない

2.promptHint: 旧脚本从「天经地义的事实」变成「他自己的东西」——他亲口认领它（它当年保护过他），或明确说它已经不再是我；认领的那一刻，松动就开始了

label.en: The old script, claimed as yours
label.ja: 古いスクリプトを引き取っている

hint.en: It turns from “an obvious fact” into “something of mine” — you claim it out loud (it once protected you), or say clearly it is no longer you. The moment you claim it, the loosening begins
hint.zh-CN: 它从「天经地义的事实」变成「我自己的东西」——你亲口认领它（它当年保护过你），或明确说它已经不再是我。认领的那一刻，松动就开始了
hint.zh-TW: 它從「天經地義的事實」變成「我自己的東西」——你親口認領它（它當年保護過你），或明確說它已經不再是我。認領的那一刻，鬆動就開始了
hint.ja: それが「あたりまえの事実」から「自分のもの」になる——古いスクリプトを自分のものだと口にするか（あの頃は自分を守ってくれた）、もう自分ではないとはっきり言えること。引き取ったその瞬間から、ゆるみがはじまる

2.promptHint: 允许真的在他身上发生过——为自己破过一次例、放自己一马，或改写过一句内在台词，体感松了一点（心虚、做砸都算，那说明碰到了旧脚本）；做过什么是证据，「允许了自己」才是标准

label.en: Having truly allowed yourself
label.ja: 自分を許せている

hint.en: Permission has really happened in you: you broke one small rule for yourself, gave yourself a break, or rewrote a line in your head — and felt it loosen (guilt or fumbling counts; it means you touched the old script). The act is only evidence; the allowance itself is the bar
hint.zh-CN: 允许真的在你身上发生过：为自己破过一次例、放自己一马，或改写一句内在台词，体感松了一点——心虚、做砸都算，那说明碰到了旧脚本。破例只是证据，「允许了自己」才是标准
hint.zh-TW: 允許真的在你身上發生過：為自己破過一次例、放自己一馬，或改寫一句內在台詞，體感鬆了一點——心虛、做砸都算，那說明碰到了舊腳本。破例只是證據，「允許了自己」才是標準
hint.ja: 許しが本当に起きたこと——自分のために小さな掟をひとつ破る、自分を解放する、心の中のせりふをひとつ書き替える。少しゆるんだ体感があればいい（後ろめたさや失敗も、古いスクリプトに触れた証拠）。破ったこと自体は証拠で、「自分を許した」ことが基準

2.promptHint: 他的话语里看得见松动——「我可以选择」「我想试试」开始替代「必须/应该/不敢」；话语是内心松紧的体温计

label.en: “I can choose” replacing “must”
label.ja: ことばに「選べる」が現れている

hint.en: Your words show the loosening — “I can choose” and “I want to try” starting to replace “must / should / dare not”. Words are the gauge of how tight or loose it is inside
hint.zh-CN: 话语里看得见松动——「我可以选择」「我想试试」开始替代「必须、应该、不敢」；话语是内心松紧的体温计
hint.zh-TW: 話語裡看得見鬆動——「我可以選擇」「我想試試」開始替代「必須、應該、不敢」；話語是內心鬆緊的體溫計
hint.ja: ことばにゆるみが見える——「選べる」「試してみたい」が「〜しなきゃ／すべき／無理」に代わって現れる。ことばは内面のゆるみの体温計

3.promptHint: 新做法在他的日子里稳定下来——与钱打交道时自然用它，不再靠硬撑和提醒；做过几轮只是证据，稳定成日常才是标准

label.en: The new way woven into your ordinary days
label.ja: 新しいやり方が日常になっている

hint.en: The new way has settled into your days — you use it naturally with money, without white-knuckling or reminders. Rounds done are only evidence; becoming ordinary is the bar
hint.zh-CN: 新做法在你的日子里稳定下来——与钱打交道时自然用它，不再靠硬撑和提醒。做过几轮只是证据，稳定成日常才是标准
hint.zh-TW: 新做法在你的日子裡穩定下來——與錢打交道時自然用它，不再靠硬撐和提醒。做過幾輪只是證據，穩定成日常才是標準
hint.ja: 新しいやり方が自分の日々に安定していること——お金と接するとき、無理に支えたり思い出したりしなくても自然に使えている。何周やったかは証拠で、日常になったことが基準

3.promptHint: 他能自己看见变化——不用别人告诉他，他自己说得出「哪里不一样了」；有变化、没变化、说不清都算，只要是自己的观察

label.en: Seeing the change for yourself
label.ja: 変化を自分で見えている

hint.en: You can see the change yourself — without being told, you can say “what's different now”. Changed, unchanged, or can't tell — all count, as long as it is your own observation
hint.zh-CN: 你能自己看见变化——不用别人告诉你，你自己说得出「哪里不一样了」。有变化、没变化、说不清都算，只要是自己的观察
hint.zh-TW: 你能自己看見變化——不用別人告訴你，你自己說得出「哪裡不一樣了」。有變化、沒變化、說不清都算，只要是自己的觀察
hint.ja: 変化を自分で見えていること——人に言われなくても「どこが違うか」を自分のことばで言える。変わった／変わらない／わからない、どれも自分の観察なら

practices.body:
# 允许清单第一周（示例笔记，可删）

这周我把允许清单落地了，写下来的是三件小事：给自己点一次贵 10 块的外卖、
下班后有一晚不碰任何"正事"、给爸妈买东西时不比价。

实际做了两件。外卖那单很顺利，付钱的时候手没抖，真正卡住的是"不碰正事"
那一晚——坐到沙发上心慌，最后还是打开了电脑。第二天才意识到，对我来说
"闲着"比"花钱"更难。

体感记录：花钱的允许几乎没阻力，休息的允许阻力很大。这个发现比我预想的
有用了——原来我的"不配"不在钱的数额上，在"我不配闲着"上。
